A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including the revised and added appendix material.

before.justification: v1 reports original multilingual caption analyses, human captioning and translation evaluations, and GIT finetuning results in Sections 3–4 and Appendices C–D.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and additionally reports GPT-4 vision caption examples and further qualitative cases in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The translation, scene-graph parsing and canonicalization, four semantic-coverage measures, and GIT finetuning procedure remain unchanged. The additional GPT-4 vision examples do not revise the proposed analysis method.

E1.justification: Both versions use Crossmodal and Visual Genome, the same seven languages, and the same US-English/Japan-Japanese human study. The added examples concern existing datasets, languages, and image-captioning requirements.

E2.justification: BLIP2 and GIT remain the English comparator models in the scene-graph comparisons, and the monolingual/multilingual finetuning comparisons retain their membership. GPT-4 vision appears only through illustrative captions, without joining these baseline comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix D.9 adds a qualitative model configuration: GPT-4 vision captions six Visual Genome images in English and Chinese, shown in Table 19. The existing caption-sampling settings, human studies, 1.8k/1.8k training–evaluation split, and SPICE evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 16 revises the cases illustrating undocumented Visual Genome objects, retaining the wheelchair example and expanding from three cases to eight. Tables 19–20 add qualitative examples of language-dependent caption content, including GPT-4 vision outputs. Existing supplementary analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The significance reporting in Tables 3 and 6, translation-quality dispersion of 4.68 ± 0.60, and Table 9 statistical summaries are unchanged. The added examples introduce no repeated-run information, uncertainty estimates, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: The established numerical tables and plotted results are unchanged, including SPICE scores in Tables 7, 17, and 18. Table 16 revises the illustrated missing-object findings, while Tables 19–20 add GPT-4 and Vertex caption outputs. These are additional qualitative results.

T1.justification: The scene-graph definitions, information-gain and intersection expressions, coverage definitions, and mathematical condition used to interpret finetuning remain unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The central multilingual-coverage and finetuning claims remain. The introduction qualifies model differences as 'often reflected,' and the conclusion removes claimed implications for segmentation and image generation. The 'inversion of the curse of multilinguality' framing leaves the conclusion but remains in Appendix A.

C2.justification: Section 3 changes the conclusion that the objectivity assumption 'does not hold' to 'may not hold.' Section 3.1 recasts the human study from verification to limited support. These qualify the interpretation of unchanged evidence; Appendix B's detailed limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Translation prompts, multilingual LLaVA prompt templates, parser information, and human-study instructions are retained. The added GPT-4 examples provide no new generation prompts, hyperparameters, hardware details, or code/data access instructions.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds WIT, Erdem et al.'s survey, and Liu et al.'s work on reasoning across languages and cultures. Citations to Kirillov et al., Sun et al., and Ramesh et al. (2021) disappear with the conclusion's broader application claims. The principal research positioning remains.

P1.justification: The introduction and related work receive local wording and paragraph edits, the conclusion is shortened, and Appendices D.9–D.10 are added. Affiliation and review-header text also change. The overall section order and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 16 is redesigned with larger images and explicit extra-object lists. Tables 19–20 add multilingual caption displays, and Tables 17–18 move to a separate page. Figures 1–5 and the established quantitative table designs remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves evidential caution by qualifying categorical interpretations in Sections 3–3.1. Expanded Table 16 and new Tables 19–20 make qualitative evidence easier to inspect. The gains are limited: Table 16 loses some explanatory commentary, GPT-4 generation settings remain unspecified, and stronger framing persists in Appendix A. The unchanged methods and quantitative results support a limited overall improvement.
